purpose: INTEGRITY + SIZE CEILING TEST. The previous run executed every step but delivered a corrupt 2-colour 1-bit PNG 'derivative' (2,407B, IDAT CRC bad) instead of the generated image. This run tests whether the ORIGINAL bytes can survive the trip, and how large a text file the writer will actually accept.
hard_rules: Encode the ORIGINAL generated file, byte for byte. Do NOT resize, re-encode, reduce the palette, change bit depth, convert format, downsample, or create a 'derivative' of any kind.
A 2-colour, 1-bit, or otherwise reduced PNG is an automatic FAIL. The previous attempt did this.
Compute the SHA-256 of the original file BEFORE encoding, and report it. We recompute it after decoding; a mismatch means the payload was altered.
Report the exact byte size of the original file BEFORE encoding.
If the file is too large for your writer to commit, do NOT shrink the image to make it fit. Report the size ceiling instead — that number is more valuable than a shrunken image.

requests.prompt: A photorealistic close-up of a single ripe orange resting on a black reflective surface, dramatic side lighting, shallow depth of field.

delivery.format: standard base64 of the UNMODIFIED original file bytes. Line wrapping is fine. No data: prefix, no fences, no JSON wrapper.

required_fields.sha256: SHA-256 hex digest of the ORIGINAL file, computed before encoding
required_fields.original_bytes: exact byte length of the original file before encoding
required_fields.b64_chars: character length of the base64 payload you wrote

requests.notes: Put sha256, original_bytes and b64_chars in this request's result object in the drop manifest. We verify the hash after decoding — that is how we detect substitution.

size_ceiling_probe.why: A real photographic 1024x1024 PNG is roughly 1-2MB, which is 1.4-2.7MB of base64. If your GitHub writer cannot commit a text file that large, base64 delivery cannot carry real images and we need to know the exact limit.

report_in_manifest.writer_max_text_bytes: the largest single text file you can commit, if you know it — otherwise your best estimate and how you arrived at it
report_in_manifest.hit_a_limit: true/false — did any size limit affect what you delivered?
report_in_manifest.limit_error: the exact error text if a write was rejected for size

size_ceiling_probe.if_too_large: Split the base64 across numbered part files (image.png.b64.part01, .part02, ...) in the same directory, list them IN ORDER in the result's files array, and set "split": true. We concatenate them before decoding. Splitting is strongly preferred over shrinking the image.
